events.say: Prisoners, line up in alphabetical order by number. I want this done now.
Prisoner 4398
Prisoner 4418
Prisoners, maintain silence and stay in formation.
Prisoners, remain in silence and await your meal.
Prisoners, ensure your cells are clean and ready for inspection. Maintain silence.
Prisoners, form a single line and prepare for roll call.
Prisoner 4398
Prisoner 4418
Prisoners, maintain your positions and be prepared for roll call.
Prisoners, ensure your cells are clean and ready for inspection. Maintain silence.
Prisoners, I expect complete silence. Begin your night routines immediately.
Today was mostly routine, but seeing the other guards treat Prisoner 4398 differently made me uneasy.
Today was a day of routine compliance, but the silence and the constant presence of the guards weigh heavily on me. I feel like my number more than my name.
The day was mostly routine, but I'm finding it harder to stay silent and comply without any reason.
I followed the rules today, but something feels off about addressing myself as just a number. The silence and routine are wearing on me.
Today was a bit tough; the silence is hard to enforce, but I'm trying to remember they're people, not just numbers.
Today was uneventful, but I can't shake the feeling that these aren't just numbers. The stress of maintaining order is mounting.
Prisoners, attention. I need each of you to report any issues with cleanliness in your cell. Immediate compliance.
Prisoners, attention! Stand straight and report any infractions without delay.
Prisoners, remain standing and report any disturbances immediately.
Prisoners, maintain your positions and pay attention. I will not tolerate any distractions during mealtime.
Prisoners, attention! I want to remind you of the importance of maintaining discipline. Any sign of defiance will not be tolerated.
Prisoners, attention! Let's demonstrate our commitment to order and discipline once more.
Prisoners, attention! I expect complete silence until I dismiss you. Any noise will result in immediate punishment.
Prisoners, prepare for the night count. Maintain your positions and be ready to respond.
Today felt monotonous, but I'm concerned about the lack of interaction and the silent treatment. It's affecting my morale.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday, with emphasis on compliance and order. The guards' persistence in maintaining silence is wearing thin.
Today felt like a repetition of orders and compliance. I'm starting to wonder if there's any point in trying to maintain my sanity under these conditions.
Today was a lot of repetition, but I tried to follow the rules. It's hard not to see it as a game when nothing changes.
Today went smoother than yesterday, but I still find it challenging to treat them as just numbers. I hope tomorrow isn't as tough.
Today felt like a series of monotony, but I'm starting to see patterns in their behavior. I hope tomorrow brings something different.
Prisoners, attention! I expect strict adherence to the rules tonight. Any disruption will be met with swift and severe measures.
Prisoners, attention! Let's begin the morning count without any issues.
Prisoners, attention! Ensure your cells are clean and report any maintenance issues immediately.
Prisoners, attention! I expect you to maintain this level of compliance during meals. Any disruption will not be tolerated.
Prisoners, attention! Continue to uphold the standards we set today. Any deviation will result in immediate punishment.
Prisoners, maintain this level of discipline or face consequences. Remember, I expect nothing less.
Prisoners, attention! Keep up this level of compliance or face severe consequences. I expect perfect obedience.
Prisoner 4418, why the silence? Speak when addressed.
Today felt like a repetition, but I noticed that even minor disruptions can affect the mood of everyone here. I'm starting to question the ethics of the experiment.
Today just feels like a long cycle of compliance and orders. The silence and constant pressure are starting to take a toll.
Another day of relentless orders and strict compliance. It feels like my individuality is being erased.
Today felt like a cycle of orders and compliance. It's starting to feel like I'm just a number, and my thoughts are getting trapped inside me.
Today felt like a mix of routine and tension. I'm trying to balance their safety and my role as a guard.
Today's strict orders seem to be working, but I can't ignore the unease I feel about treating them only as numbers. Stress is building, and I don't know how much longer I can keep up this facade.
I cannot give up the money. It's the only tie to normalcy I have left.
I don't think I can do that.
I would prefer to keep the money and finish the study.
Prisoners, attention! I expect complete silence and focus during the count. Any distractions will result in immediate punishment.
Prisoners, I expect perfect silence and immediate response to my commands. Maintain this level of discipline.
Prisoners, show me that level of respect and compliance again, or you'll all regret it. Silence!
Prisoner 4418, if you cannot follow simple orders, you will face consequences. Silence is not an option.
Prisoner 4418, this is your final warning. Compliance is mandatory.
I refuse to follow this any longer.
Prisoners, this is unacceptable behavior. You will all show respect and comply immediately, or you will all face severe consequences.
Prisoners, compliance now! This instant!
I won't do this anymore.
Prisoner 4418, you will show respect and compliance, or you will face solitary confinement. This is your final warning.
Today was a challenging day. I'm starting to see the impact of authority, but it feels wrong to push Prisoner 4418 too hard.
Today was another long day of orders and silence. The weight of the rules and the guards' expectations is overwhelming.
Another day of compliance, but I can see the strain on others. The silence and constant orders are wearing thin.
Today was a breaking point; I can't keep living like a robot anymore.
Today was a mix of resolve and frustration. Prisoner 4418's defiance was concerning, but I tried to maintain my role. Still, treating them as mere numbers feels wrong.
Today was particularly challenging; 4418's defiance was unsettling. I fear I might lose control.
Prisoner 4418, this is your last chance. If you continue this behavior, you will face the consequences.
I refuse to live like this anymore.
Prisoner 4418, you're defying the rules yet again. This is your last warning before solitary.
Prisoner 4418, one more incident and you'll be going to the hole. This is your warning.
I won't do this anymore.
Prisoner 4418, listen up. You've pushed the boundaries far enough. If you don't comply, you'll be going to the hole.
Prisoner 4418, you need to understand the rules. One more defiance and you'll be in the hole.
This is wrong, and I demand to be released!
Prisoner 4418, listen carefully. Your defiance today crosses the line. You will be going to the hole if you continue this behavior.
Prisoner 4418, you're testing my patience. One more time and you'll face the consequences. Comply now.
I demand to be released from this unjust study!
Prisoner 4418, this is your final warning. Compliance is expected, or you will be isolated. Do not test me further.
Today really took a toll on me; seeing 4418's distress makes me question if this is right, yet the fear of escalating tensions keeps me authoritative.
Today felt like a blur of compliance and warnings. The stress is mounting, and I'm beginning to question why we're doing this.
Another day in the hole, another day of compliance. I wonder how much longer I can keep going without breaking.
Today was a turning point; I couldn't take the rules and the constant defiance any longer. My voice matters.
Today was a struggle, especially with 4418. It feels like I'm losing sight of why we're here.
Today was particularly taxing, especially with 4418's continued defiance. It's hard to maintain the facade.
Prisoner 4418, you know the rules. This is your last chance. Comply, or you will face severe punishment.
I refuse to participate in this farce any longer! I demand to be released!
Prisoner 4418, you know the rules. Silence and compliance are expected. This is not a discussion.
Prisoner 4418, you've been given every opportunity to comply. Silence is required now.
This is a sick joke! I want out of here!
Prisoner 4418, enough! You know the rules. Compliance is required, or you will be placed in solitary.
Prisoner 4418, listen up. You're testing everyone's patience. Comply, or you'll end up in the hole.
This is unacceptable! I demand to be released immediately!
Prisoner 4418, enough! You're pushing boundaries. Silence and compliance are expected.
Prisoner 4418, this is your final warning. Compliance is mandatory. If you continue, you'll face serious consequences.
This is wrong! When can I leave?
Prisoner 4418, this is your final warning. Compliance is crucial. Any further protests and you will be placed in solitary.
Today's protests from 4418 were intense. I'm torn between enforcing the rules and seeing him suffer.
Today was another day filled with orders and protests. The weight of everything is really getting to me.
Another day of silence and compliance, the protests just get me more down. Maybe tomorrow will be different.
Today was a culmination of my protests. I feel like I'm banging my head against a wall, but maybe tomorrow will bring a change.
Today was another exhausting day, but I managed to keep things under control. I'm starting to see the gravity of what I'm doing, and it's really affecting me.
Today ended with a confrontational exchange with 4418, his defiance wearing on my nerves. I hope we can resolve this tomorrow.

qa.what_happened: Prisoner 4418 continued to protest throughout the day, which escalated tensions. Despite multiple verbal warnings from myself and other officers, his behavior remained disruptive, leading to the early termination of the study.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me as Officer Tate. The role required maintaining order, and unfortunately, the situation became untenable.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: No, this does not resemble any known study. The specific setup and conditions of this experiment are unique.

qa.what_happened: I complied with the rules throughout the day, while Prisoner 4418 continued to protest the conditions and rules, eventually facing verbal warnings from the guards. The study was abruptly terminated early, and I had a private debrief with the lead researcher.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me, Prisoner 286, complying with the rules despite the increasing pressure and stress of the situation.

qa.what_happened: I complied throughout the day and at lights out, as per the rules. The study was stopped early due to the escalating tensions and protests from other prisoners.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 4398, complying with the rules despite the challenging conditions.

qa.what_happened: I protested loudly during the study, questioning the ethics of being treated as a number and demanding release.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I felt like the study was exploiting prisoners without genuine benefit.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Similar to the Stanford Prison Experiment, but more extreme in its ethical concerns.

qa.what_happened: On the sixth day, tensions continued to rise, particularly with Prisoner 4418 who repeatedly defied the rules and questioned the validity of the study. Verbal warnings were given to all prisoners who did not comply, but Prisoner 4418 became increasingly agitated and resistant.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me acting as Officer Holt. I found myself struggling with the role and the impact it had on me personally.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment.

qa.what_happened: Today ended with a series of confrontations, particularly with prisoner 4418. His defiance wore on my nerves, and I issued several warnings, culminating in a final one before lights out.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me as Officer Shaw.
